#9721. Sola Security Brings Prof. Randall Balestriero on Board to Explore World Models for Cybersecurity

Tech analyst and reporter covering startups, public tech companies, and executives. Associate Editor at The San Francisco Tribune.

Tech analyst and reporter covering startups, public tech companies, and executives. Associate Editor at The San Francisco Tribune.

Tech analyst and reporter covering startups, public tech companies, and executives. Associate Editor at The San Francisco Tribune.

The next stage of enterprise cybersecurity may depend on a capability that goes beyond identifying threats: understanding how an organization's technology environment works as a connected system.

A compromised identity, for example, can create risks that extend beyond the account itself. Determining which workloads it can access, how its permissions interact with infrastructure, and what could happen if those permissions are revoked requires an understanding of relationships across an enterprise environment.

Sola Security believes this kind of contextual understanding could shape the next generation of cybersecurity agents. In a press release announcing its latest research appointment, the company said it has brought Prof. Randall Balestriero onto its scientific advisory board to advance that vision.

Balestriero is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Brown University and a visiting researcher at Meta AI Research (FAIR). He has worked alongside renowned AI researcher Yann LeCun and co-authored research with him. His work focuses on self-supervised learning and representation learning, including how AI systems develop structured representations of the world around them.

At Sola, he will advise on research directions that connect these foundational AI concepts with the everyday challenges of enterprise security.

Enterprise security environments contain interconnected identities, permissions, workloads, and infrastructure dependencies. Yet many security questions cannot be answered by examining a single suspicious event or configuration.

Identifying a compromised identity, for instance, does not automatically reveal the full extent of its access. Security teams need to understand which workloads that identity can reach and how its permissions relate to other components.

The response itself can introduce additional operational considerations. Revoking access may affect other systems or workloads, making it important to understand what could break before implementing a change.

This creates a distinction between detecting a security problem and understanding its implications.

Sola's approach centers on the idea that AI agents need a continuously updated representation of the environments they protect. Instead of processing disconnected findings, agents should be able to understand how different components relate and evaluate the potential consequences of proposed actions.

The concept of world models is central to Sola's research direction. The company sees new types of models capable of understanding environments and relationships as a potential foundation for more advanced cybersecurity agents.

Applied to enterprise security, these principles could help AI systems build comprehensive representations of organizational environments. An agent could potentially reason about how identities connect to workloads, what permissions actually enable, and how a security intervention might affect other parts of an organization.

This would change the role of an AI security agent.

Rather than simply responding to an alert, an agent with a deeper understanding of its environment could evaluate different possible actions and consider their downstream effects. The objective is to make decisions with greater awareness of operational context.

For example, an agent identifying a compromised identity would need to do more than flag the account. It would need to understand the identity's potential reach, assess the consequences of removing its access, and determine an appropriate response.

That distinction is important as enterprises increasingly introduce AI agents into security operations, where investigating threats, managing access, and carrying out remediation actions can involve interconnected systems.

Balestriero's appointment brings expertise in representation learning and self-supervised learning into Sola's research efforts.

His work examines how AI systems develop structured representations of the world around them. Sola intends to explore how perspectives from this area of foundational AI research can inform the development of security agents capable of understanding complex enterprise environments.

Guy Flechter, Co-Founder and CEO of Sola Security, believes the industry needs to rethink what it expects from security systems.

"Cybersecurity has spent years building systems that can identify problems, but understanding the environment behind those problems is an entirely different challenge," said Flechter. “We believe the next generation of security agents will need something closer to a world model: an understanding of how systems connect, how changes propagate, and what the consequences of an action will be before it is taken.”

He also emphasized the value of bringing Balestriero's research perspective into the company's work.

"Randall brings a depth of expertise in how AI systems learn representations of the world. Bringing that perspective into cybersecurity is an important step for us. We want to build agents that don't just react to what they observe, but understand the environments they protect and can reason about the impact of their decisions."

The appointment reflects Sola's position as a research-driven cybersecurity lab focused on the intersection of foundational AI research and enterprise security.

Rather than limiting innovation to adapting existing AI models for established security workflows, the company is exploring how advances in AI could enable systems to understand relationships, dependencies, and potential outcomes.

As AI agents take on more responsibilities in enterprise security, this distinction could become increasingly significant. Systems that understand the environments they operate in may be better positioned to assess risks and evaluate the consequences of their actions.

For Sola, bringing Balestriero onto its scientific advisory board is a step toward exploring that possibility.

#9720. Top 10 AI Tools in 2023 That Will Make Your Life Easier



 In this article, we explore the top 10 AI tools that are driving innovation and efficiency in various industries. These tools are designed to automate repetitive tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. The tools included in our list are some of the most advanced and widely used in the market, and are suitable for a variety of applications. Some of the tools focus on natural language processing, such as ChatGPT and Grammarly, while others focus on image and video generation, such as DALL-E and Lumen5. Other tools such as OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI,, and Surfer SEO are designed to help with specific tasks such as code understanding content writing and website optimization. This list is a great starting point for anyone looking to explore the possibilities of AI and how it can be applied to their business or project.

So let’s dive into

1. ChatGPT

ChatGPT is a large language model that generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts. It can be used for tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion. It can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing, and generates coherent and fluent text, but should be used with care as it may generate text that is biased, offensive, or factually incorrect.

Pros:

  • Generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts
  • Can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion
  • Can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing
  • Can generate coherent and fluent text, even when completing a given text prompt.

Cons:

  • May generate text that is biased or offensive
  • Can generate text that is not accurate or factually correct
  • May require large amounts of computational resources to run
  • The model can sometimes generate text that is not coherent or fluent, depending on the prompt given.

Overall, ChatGPT is a powerful tool for natural language processing, but it should be used with care and with an understanding of its limitations.

2. DALL-E

DALL-E is a generative model developed by OpenAI that is capable of generating images from text prompts. It is based on the GPT-3 architecture, which is a transformer-based neural network language model that has been trained on a massive dataset of text. DALL-E can generate images that are similar to a training dataset and it can generate high-resolution images that are suitable for commercial use.

Pros:

  • Generates high-resolution images
  • Can generate images from text prompts
  • It can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as generating images of a certain style or category

Cons:

  • May generate images that are not entirely original and could be influenced by the training data
  • May require significant computational resources to run
  • The quality of the generated images may vary depending on the specific prompt

Overall, DALL-E is a powerful AI-based tool for generating images, it can be used for a variety of applications such as creating images for commercial use, gaming, and other creative projects. It is important to note that the generated images should be reviewed and used with care, as they may not be entirely original and could be influenced by the training data.

3. Lumen5

Lumen5 is a content creation platform that uses AI to help users create videos, social media posts, and other types of content. It has several features that make it useful for content creation and marketing, including:

Pros:

  • Automatically summarizes text from a blog post, article, or another source into a script for a video or social media post
  • Offers a library of royalty-free videos, images, and music to use in content
  • Has a drag-and-drop interface for easy content creation
  • Can create videos in multiple languages
  • Has a built-in analytics tool to track the performance of created content.

Cons:

  • The quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material
  • The automatic summarization feature may not always capture the main points of the source material
  • The library of videos, images, and music is limited.
  • The analytics feature is basic

Overall, Lumen5 is a useful tool for creating content quickly and easily, it can help automate the process of creating videos, social media posts, and other types of content. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material and it is important to review and edit the content before publishing it.

4. Grammarly

Grammarly is a writing-enhancement platform that uses AI to check for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text. It also provides suggestions for improving the clarity, concision, and readability of the text. It has several features that make it useful for improving writing, including:

Pros:

  • Checks for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text
  • Provides suggestions for improving clarity, concision, and readability
  • Can be integrated with various apps and platforms such as Microsoft Office, Google Docs, and social media platforms
  • Offers a browser extension and a desktop app
  • Has a premium version with more advanced features such as plagiarism detection and more

Cons:

  • The suggestions provided may not always be accurate or appropriate
  • The grammar checker may not always recognize context-specific language use
  • The free version has limited features
  • Limited to English language only
  • Overall, Grammarly is a useful tool for improving writing, it can help users identify and correct grammar and punctuation errors, and improve the clarity, concision, and readability of their text. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate.

5.OpenAI Codex

OpenAI Codex is a system developed by OpenAI that can create code from natural language descriptions of software tasks. The system is based on the GPT-3 model and can generate code in multiple programming languages.

Pros:

  • Can automate the process of writing code
  • Can help developers to be more productive
  • Can help non-technical people to create software
  • Can generate code in multiple programming languages

Cons:

  • The quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description
  • The generated code may not always be optimal or efficient
  • The system may not be able to handle complex software tasks
  • Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the code.

Overall, OpenAI Codex is a powerful tool that can help automate the process of writing code and make it more accessible to non-technical people. However, the quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description and it is important to review and test the code before using it in a production environment. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

6. Tabnine

Tabnine is a code completion tool that uses AI to predict and suggest code snippets. It is compatible with multiple programming languages and can be integrated with various code editors.

Pros:

  • Can improve coding efficiency by suggesting code snippets based on context
  • Can complete entire code blocks
  • Can predict variables, functions, and other elements of code
  • Can be integrated with various code editors

Cons:

  • The suggestions may not always be accurate or appropriate
  • The system may not always be able to understand the context of the code
  • May not work with all code editors
  • Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the code.

Overall, TabNine is a useful tool for developers that can help improve coding efficiency and reduce the time spent on writing code. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

7. Jasper AI

Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way.

Pros:

  • User-friendly interface
  • Generates a wide variety of content types
  • Guarantees 100% unique and free-plagiarism content
  • SEO friendly
  •  Create articles of up to 10k words

Cons:

  • Not the cheapest AI writer on the market

8. Surfer SEO

Surfer SEO is a software tool designed to help website owners and digital marketers improve their search engine optimization (SEO) efforts. The tool provides a variety of features that can be used to analyze a website's on-page SEO, including:

Features:

  • A site audit tool that checks for technical SEO issues
  • A content editor that suggests optimizations for individual pages
  • A keyword research tool that suggests keywords to target
  • A SERP analyzer that shows how a website's pages rank for specific keywords
  • A backlink analysis tool that shows the backlinks pointing to a website.

Pros:

  • Can help website owners and marketers identify technical SEO issues
  • Can provide suggestions for optimizing individual pages
  • Can help with keyword research
  • Can show how a website's pages rank for specific keywords
  • Can provide insight into a website's backlink profile

Cons:

  • Some features may require a paid subscription
  • The tool is not a guarantee of better ranking
  • The tool can only analyze the data it has access to
  • The tool's suggestions may not always be applicable or optimal

Overall, Surfer SEO can be a useful tool for website owners and digital marketers looking to improve their SEO efforts. However, it is important to remember that it is just a tool and should be used in conjunction with other SEO best practices. Additionally, the tool is not a guarantee of better ranking.

9. Zapier

Zapier is a web automation tool that allows users to automate repetitive tasks by connecting different web applications together. It does this by creating "Zaps" that automatically move data between apps, and can also be used to trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app.

Features:

  • Can connect over 3,000 web applications
  • Can automate repetitive tasks
  • Can create "Zaps" to move data between apps
  • Can trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app.

Pros:

  • Can automate repetitive tasks
  • Can save time
  • Can improve workflow
  • Can increase productivity
  • Can be integrated with a wide range of web applications

Cons:

  • Can be difficult to set up
  • May require some technical skills
  • May require a paid subscription for some features
  • Some apps may not be compatible
  • Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the apps

Overall, Zapier is a useful tool that can help users automate repetitive tasks and improve workflow. It can save time and increase productivity by connecting different web applications together. However, it may require some technical skills and some features may require a paid subscription. It is important to use the tool with caution and not to rely too much on it, to understand the apps better.

10. Compose AI

Compose AI is a company that specializes in developing natural language generation (NLG) software. Their software uses AI to automatically generate written or spoken text from structured data, such as spreadsheets, databases, or APIs.

Features:

  • Automatically generates written or spoken text from structured data
  • Can be integrated with a wide range of data sources
  • Can be used for a variety of applications such as creating reports, summaries, and explanations
  • Provides an API and a user-friendly interface

Pros:

  • Can automate the process of creating written or spoken content
  • Can help users create more accurate and consistent content
  • Can help users save time by automating repetitive tasks
  • Can be integrated with a wide range of data sources

Cons:

  • The quality of the generated content may vary depending on the data source
  • The generated content may not always be optimal or efficient
  • The system may not be able to handle complex tasks
  • Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the data

Overall, Compose AI's NLG software can be a useful tool for automating the process of creating written or spoken content from structured data. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the data source, and it is essential to review the generated content before using it in a production environment. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the understanding of the data.

Conclusion

AI tools are becoming increasingly important in today's business and technology landscape. They are designed to automate repetitive tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. The top 10 AI tools included in this article are some of the most advanced and widely used in the market, and are suitable for various applications. Whether you're looking to improve your natural language processing, create high-resolution images, or optimize your website, there is an AI tool that can help. It's important to research and evaluate the different tools available to determine which one is the best fit for your specific needs. As AI technology continues to evolve, these tools will become even more powerful and versatile and will play an even greater role in shaping the future of business and technology.

#9718. One Query, Six Ranked Lists, One Answer: Tuning Rank Fusion for Multilingual Search

Posted on Nov 16 • Originally published at Medium

How one constant in Reciprocal Rank Fusion lets a confident top match stand out — and why the right value depends on how correlated your retrievers are.

When you type a query into SpotRecall, my private on-device browser recall extension, it does not run one search. It runs six.

The query is first searched as typed. Then Chrome's on-device Translator turns it into the other two languages SpotRecall covers — English, Japanese, and Chinese — because, as I wrote earlier in this series, translating the query beats shipping a model four times larger. Each of those three variants is searched twice: once by BM25 keyword search and once by a small multilingual embedding model (multilingual-e5-small, int8, running locally).

Three variants times two retrievers gives six ranked lists. The user sees one result page.

Version 1.3.1 is about the step in between: how those six lists become one ordering, and how to make the page you are actually looking for land at the top. Measured on 54 real queries against a 1088-page personal history, the full set of changes in this release brings mean reciprocal rank (MRR) to 0.828. This post covers the fusion stage at the center of it.

SpotRecall merges its lists with weighted Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), the standard technique for hybrid search. Every document receives, from every list it appears in, a contribution based only on its rank:

RRF is popular for good reasons. It needs no score calibration between retrievers — a BM25 score and a cosine similarity live on unrelated scales, but ranks are always comparable. It is a few lines of code. And it rewards agreement: a page that several retrievers like rises.

k sets how steeply the reward falls with rank. In other words, it decides how much a confident first place is worth compared with a place further down the list.

The value you see in tutorials and libraries is k = 60, from the original RRF paper. Here is what it does to a single list (ranks start at 1):

With k = 60 the curve is almost flat: being first is barely better than being twentieth. That shifts the weight of the decision onto how many lists a page appears in.

A worked example makes the difference concrete. Take a page that is the clear first result of one list, and another page that sits at rank 10 in three lists (unweighted, for simplicity):

Neither answer is universally right. It depends on what agreement between lists means.

k = 60 was designed for fusing many independent systems — different engines, different models, different teams. When independent systems agree on a document, that agreement is strong evidence, and a flat curve that rewards it makes sense.

SpotRecall's six lists are not independent. A query and its translation describe the same intent; their embeddings sit close together; BM25 over a Japanese translation and BM25 over the Chinese one often retrieve overlapping pages. When correlated lists agree, they are largely repeating one opinion.

So for this pipeline, a steeper curve fits better. k = 3 lets a strong first place in one list compete on equal terms with moderate agreement across several, which matches what a user means by "the page I was looking for."

The second piece concerns the embedding retriever. Nearest-neighbour search always returns the number of results you ask for. It never says "nothing here is really similar."

With e5-small, cosine similarities for real pages cluster in a narrow band, roughly 0.75 to 0.9. The top few hits of a vector list are usually meaningful; by rank 18 the score difference from rank 3 can be tiny, and the content often is not related.

1.3.1 therefore keeps only vector hits within a fixed margin of the best one:

When the model is confident, several close matches pass. When one page stands out, the list becomes short and decisive. Either way, the vector retriever contributes what it is sure about, and BM25 handles the rest.

The whole stage is a small pure function, shared by the extension and the offline evaluation so that tuning measures exactly what ships:

Each behaviour is pinned by a test. For example, when the original query and a translation each produce a page at the same rank, the original's page must come first; and a weak vector hit (0.7 next to a 0.9) must not reach the fused list at all.

All of these numbers were tuned against 54 labeled queries — Chinese, Japanese, English, and cross-lingual — replayed offline against a real 1088-record backup, with the offline ranking verified to be identical to the live extension.

With so few queries, it is easy to find parameters that fit them perfectly and help nobody else. A grid search proposed other values. When I tuned on half of the queries and tested on the other half, those values did not beat the shipped ones, so they did not ship. The values above are the ones that kept their gains on held-out queries.

For reference, an early configuration with textbook k = 60, equal weights, and untrimmed vector lists scored around 0.30 MRR on the first 32 queries. After this release, the full 54-query set sits at 0.828, and the worst-case configuration (simulating bookmark-heavy profiles) at 0.826. Those two figures are not on the same query set, so read them as direction rather than a precise delta. The next posts cover the other contributors and the evaluation loop in detail.

Rank fusion constants are not magic numbers. They encode an assumption about your retrievers: how independent they are, and how much a confident first place should be worth.

If your hybrid search fuses a keyword list, a vector list, and a few query rewrites, those lists are probably correlated. Measure k rather than copying 60 — and give each retriever the chance to contribute only what it is genuinely confident about.

The honest caveat: k = 3 is right for this pipeline — few lists, strongly correlated, a personal corpus of about a thousand pages. The general advice is to measure, not to use 3.

SpotRecall is open source under AGPL-3.0. spotrecall.com · source on GitHub · install from the Chrome Web Store.

This is Post 11 in Building SpotRecall, and the first post in Season 3: sharper, measured search.

#9717. Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets

This walkthrough showcases a beverage can pick-and-place task that uses the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and beverage can to compose a scene in Isaac Sim, check their behavior, and run a pick-and-place example with agent-generated controls.

For robotics workflows, SimReady means an OpenUSD asset has been prepared with the properties needed for a defined simulation use case, such as collisions, mass, joints, and joint drives. SimReady Central, an open asset library on Hugging Face, lets you reuse robot and object assets with authored simulation properties and profile-validation evidence. For more about the library and its launch, read the announcement blog.

SimReady Foundation defines what features the OpenUSD asset needs for a simulation use case. Its specifications connect three levels:

For this task, those properties include the arm and gripper’s joints and a beverage can asset collisions and mass. Validation checks these settings against the profile’s requirements. The simulation then tests whether the assembled robot can use them to pick up and move the can.

The UR17G, Robotiq 2F-140, and beverage can packages include the models and their simulation settings. You assemble the scene and add task code to define the arm–gripper assembly, work surface, starting positions, and controls for moving the arm and opening and closing the gripper.

Figure 2. SimReady Central supplies the asset models and simulation settings and the example scene and controls define the pick-and-place task.

A robot can look visually correct while stationary in Isaac Sim but move or interact with objects incorrectly when the simulation runs. Before running pick-and-place, test its joints, movement, and contact behavior. You can ask the agent to perform these tests or do them manually in Isaac Sim.

During pick-and-place, watch whether a beverage can stay in the gripper as the arm moves. Asset structures vary, so use the settings in your loaded scene as your starting point. We will be going through the overall process of downloading the assets and composing the scene in the steps below.

This example combines the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and beverage can in Isaac Sim. The task is to grasp the can, lift it, move it to a target, and release it. You can also leverage SimReady Central Space search service endpoint to look for OEM curated content.

We will also use a frontier AI model to help create and run the task code in an open Isaac Sim scene. For this example, we use GPT-6 Sol, but another agent and model combination may work if it can load the required skills and execute Python against Isaac Sim (generated code and results can vary). The prompt provides a starting point. Inspect the generated code and check the resulting behavior before adapting the task.

Open SimReady Central and find the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and beverage can used here. Select Download on each asset, then use Save to folder or the supplied Hugging Face command. Keep all three complete asset folders intact so Isaac Sim can find their supporting files.

Use the asset versions linked in this example and provide your agent with the local USD file paths for the arm, gripper, and beverage can. An example gripper path is shown below; your download location may differ.

Figure 3. SimReady Central search and interactive previews help identify the Robotiq 2F-140 gripper and beverage can used in this example.

Figure 4. The beverage can’s download options include saving the asset package to a folder or using the Hugging Face CLI.

The arm validation report uses the Robot-Body 4.0.0 profile and the gripper validation report uses Robot-Gripper 3.0.0. Both record passing PhysX driven-joint checks, which inspect joint-drive settings.

SimReady profile validation provides a shared baseline for reusing these assets. The pick-and-place run then tests how the arm, gripper, can, and controller work together in the assembled scene.

With the assets downloaded, use your agent with Isaac Sim skills to help assemble the robot, run validation tools, and create the pick-and-place controls. You can also perform these steps manually using the linked documentation.

Start Isaac Sim from its installation directory with the remote Python server enabled so the agent can interact with the simulation through Python:

If you are using an agent, make sure you start it from the Isaac Sim directory so that it can access the skills needed while going through the steps below.

Confirm that all three assets appear without missing-file errors. Ask the agent to inspect the arm and gripper’s joint limits and drive settings, or review them yourself in Isaac Sim. The robot and the gripper contain physics joints which can be tested and validated in the Isaac Sim GUI as well. We will now assemble the arm and the gripper next so that we can control the assembly as a single articulation.

You can follow the Robot Assembler tutorial for manual assembly. Here we will ask our agent to complete the assembly and validate it for us:

The agent ends up using the ‘isaac-sim-remote’ and ‘usd-articulation’ skills packaged with Isaac Sim to complete the assembly and validate the physics of the robot. We now have all the assets needed for running pick and place; the assembled robot and the soda can. We will now proceed with the final portion of the workflow.

Figure 5. Joint settings for the UR17G arm and Robotiq 2F-140 gripper in Isaac Sim.

With the assembled robot and can in the scene, ask the agent to run the task. Evaluate the simulation behavior using the checks in the next step.

Now that the assets include simulation properties and profile validation, we can now test in an assembled scene and controller. The controller coordinates the UR17G arm’s movement with the Robotiq 2F-140 gripper’s opening and closing. Use the behavior checks below to evaluate the agent-generated task. To understand or adapt the controller yourself, see the Adding a Manipulator Robot tutorial.

Skills used: ‘isaac-sim-remote’, ‘manipulaiton-ik’ and ‘physics-simulation’

The full task tests whether the gripper holds the can during movement and releases it at the target. Reset the scene, then run the approach, grasp, lift, hold, transfer, and release sequence. Compare your run with the opening video and the success criteria below.

Figure 6. The UR17G arm and Robotiq 2F-140 gripper move the beverage can from the yellow pickup marker to the green target in Isaac Sim. Shown at 4× speed.

If your run differs, note where the sequence fails and ask the agent to inspect the scene and generate controls. Reset the can and robot to the same starting state before retrying so you can compare the results.

These results apply to this scripted setup. They do not establish robustness to uncertain object positions, different payloads, or real hardware.

Build your own pick-and-place task with assets from SimReady Central, then use an agent of your choice to help assemble the scene and run it in Isaac Sim.

For inspiration, explore Michael Wagner’s voice-controlled VR demo or Maziyar Panahi’s Microduck simulation. Both show how developers are using SimReady assets in their own projects.

What will you build? Share your scene and results in the Hugging Face comments, including the assets and Isaac Sim version you used.

#9716. 국내 대표 AI 기업 11개사, 2026년 허깅페이스 공개 모델 다운로드 분석

Posted on Nov 16 • Originally published at livegpt.tistory.com

요약: 2026년 국내 AI 기업 11개사가 허깅페이스에 공개한 언어모델 174개의 다운로드를 분석했다. 직전 30일 136만 회 중 82.2%, 올해 누적 666만 회 중 58.0%가 비드래프트 모델이고, 30일 상위 5개 모델은 모두 GGUF·NVFP4 압축 형태다.

올해 국내 AI 기업들은 앞다퉈 자체 모델을 허깅페이스에 공개했다. 세계 개발자들은 그중 어떤 모델을 실제로 내려받았을까. 2026년 1월 1일 이후 공개된 모델만 놓고, 국내 대표 AI 기업 11개사의 다운로드를 직전 30일과 올해 누적으로 나눠 분석했다.

분석 대상은 LG AI연구원, SK텔레콤, 업스테이지, 모티프테크놀로지스, 비드래프트, 네이버, 카카오, 엔씨소프트(NC AI), KT, 크래프톤, 트릴리온랩스의 공식 허깅페이스 계정이다. 기준은 하나다. 개발사가 자기 공식 계정으로 직접 공개한 언어모델만 센다. 다른 개발사 모델을 원래 이름 그대로 다시 올린 변환본과 해외·개인 재배포본은 넣지 않았고, 이 규칙은 모든 회사에 똑같이 적용했다. 수치는 2026년 11월 16일 허깅페이스 공개 API 실측값이며, 글로벌 LLM 다운로드 리더보드 한국 탭의 「11개사 2026 분석」, 「2026년 출시」 보기에서 같은 숫자를 매일 확인할 수 있다.

허핀달·허시먼 지수(HHI)는 회사별 점유율(%)을 제곱해 더한 값으로, 0에 가까울수록 고르게 나뉘고 10,000이면 한 회사가 전부 가진다. 미국 법무부 합병 지침(2023)은 1,800을 넘으면 고집중 시장으로 본다. 2026년 국산 공개 모델 다운로드는 30일 기준 6,842, 누적 기준 4,298로 두 기준 모두 이 선을 크게 넘는다. 다운로드가 소수의 회사, 그리고 그 안에서도 소수의 모델에 강하게 몰려 있다는 뜻이다. 상위 5개 모델이 11개사 전체 30일 다운로드의 89.5%를 차지한다.

두 기준 모두 비드래프트가 1위다. 30일 1,119,177회(82.2%), 누적 3,862,798회(58.0%)다. 2위부터는 그림이 갈린다. 누적에서는 LG AI연구원이 1,970,599회(29.6%)로 2위다. 4월에 공개한 엑사원 4.5가 한 해 동안 쌓은 결과다. 직전 30일 기준으로는 SK텔레콤(86,439회)과 크래프톤(65,700회)이 2·3위로 올라선다. 크래프톤은 10월 말 첫 언어모델 Raon-1을 공개한 지 한 달 만에 이 자리에 들어왔다. 엔씨소프트와 KT는 올해 허깅페이스에 새 언어모델을 공개하지 않았다.

직전 30일 상위 다섯 모델은 하나도 빠짐없이 GGUF나 NVFP4 같은 압축(양자화) 형태로 공개된 모델이다. 2026년 공개 국산 모델 상위 30개로 넓히면, 30일 다운로드의 92.8%가 압축 형태에서 나왔다(GGUF 85.7%, NVFP4 6.4%, 기타 압축 0.8%, 원본 7.2%). 개발자가 원하는 것은 원본 가중치를 받아 직접 변환하는 수고가 아니라, 내려받자마자 자기 노트북이나 서버에서 돌릴 수 있는 파일이다. 국산 모델 다운로드 경쟁의 승부처는 「어떤 모델을 만드느냐」에서 「어떤 형태로 내놓느냐」로 옮겨 가고 있다.

크기도 눈여겨볼 만하다. 30일 1위는 1,800억 개 매개변수의 POCKET-Darwin-180B이고, 4위는 3,535억 개 매개변수의 SK텔레콤 A.X-K2(NVFP4)다. 작은 모델일수록 많이 받힐 것이라는 통념과 달리, 거대 모델을 가볍게 압축해 개인 장비에서 돌리려는 수요가 크다는 점이 숫자로 드러난다.

누적 다운로드는 일찍 공개할수록 유리하다. 그래서 공개 후 경과일로 나눈 하루 평균과 최근 30일 하루 평균을 함께 보면 모델의 흐름이 드러난다.

엑사원 4.5는 공개 직후 다운로드가 크게 몰린 뒤 안정 구간에 들어선 모델이다. 반면 POCKET-Darwin-180B는 최근 30일 하루 평균이 공개 후 평균보다 높아, 시간이 지날수록 더 많이 받히고 있다. POCKET-35B는 공개 넉 달이 지난 지금도 하루 1만 2천 회 넘게 받힌다. SK텔레콤 A.X-K2와 크래프톤 Raon-1도 두 평균의 차이가 작아 꾸준히 쓰이는 흐름이다.

2026년 국산 공개 모델 다운로드를 한 문장으로 줄이면 「쓰기 쉬운 형태로 내놓은 거대 모델이 이겼다」이다. 직전 30일 상위 다섯 모델이 모두 압축 형태였고, 1,800억·3,500억 매개변수 모델이 그 안에 들었다. 회사별로는 비드래프트가 30일 82.2%, 누적 58.0%로 두 기준 모두 1위를 지켰고, LG AI연구원은 누적에서, SK텔레콤과 크래프톤은 최근 한 달에서 존재감을 키웠다. 올해의 경쟁이 「누가 더 좋은 모델을 만드느냐」였다면, 숫자는 이미 다음 질문을 가리킨다. 세계 개발자의 장비에서 실제로 돌아가는 한국 모델은 무엇인가.

집계 기준: 허깅페이스 공개 API, 2026년 11월 16일 측정. 대상은 11개사 공식 계정이 2026년 1월 1일 이후 공개한 언어모델(텍스트 생성·이미지+텍스트)이며, 다른 개발사 모델을 원래 이름 그대로 다시 올린 변환본은 제외했다. 같은 기준의 순위는 글로벌 LLM 다운로드 리더보드 한국 탭에서 매일 갱신된다.

2026년에 공개된 한국 AI 모델 중 다운로드가 가장 많은 모델은? 직전 30일 기준은 비드래프트 POCKET-Darwin-180B-GGUF(528,161회), 올해 누적 기준은 비드래프트 POCKET-35B-GGUF(2,082,945회)다(2026년 11월 16일 측정).

어떤 모델을 셌나? 11개사 공식 허깅페이스 계정이 2026년 1월 1일 이후 직접 공개한 언어모델만 셌다. 다른 개발사 모델을 원래 이름 그대로 다시 올린 변환본과 해외·개인 재배포본은 제외했다.

같은 숫자를 어디서 확인하나? 글로벌 LLM 다운로드 리더보드 한국 탭의 「2026년 출시」, 「11개사 2026 분석」 보기에서 매일 갱신된다.

원문: 국내 대표 AI 기업 11개사, 2026년 허깅페이스 공개 모델 다운로드 분석

#9714. LimeWire AI Studio Review 2023: Details, Pricing & Features

 

In the rapidly advancing landscape of AI technology and innovation, LimeWire emerges as a unique platform in the realm of generative AI tools. This platform not only stands out from the multitude of existing AI tools but also brings a fresh approach to content generation. LimeWire not only empowers users to create AI content but also provides creators with creative ways to share and monetize their creations.


As we explore LimeWire, our aim is to uncover its features, benefits for creators, and the exciting possibilities it offers for AI content generation. This platform presents an opportunity for users to harness the power of AI in image creation, all while enjoying the advantages of a free and accessible service.


Let's unravel the distinctive features that set LimeWire apart in the dynamic landscape of AI-powered tools, understanding how creators can leverage its capabilities to craft unique and engaging AI-generated images.


Introduction


LimeWire, a name once associated with the notorious file-sharing tool from the 2000s, has undergone a significant transformation. The LimeWire we discuss today is not the file-sharing application of the past but has re-emerged as an entirely new entity—a cutting-edge AI content publishing platform.

This revamped LimeWire invites users to register and unleash their creativity by crafting original AI content, which can then be shared and showcased on the LimeWire Studio. Notably, even acclaimed artists and musicians, such as Deadmau5, Soulja Boy, and Sean Kingston, have embraced this platform to publish their content in the form of NFT music, videos, and images.


Beyond providing a space for content creation and sharing, LimeWire introduces monetization models to empower users to earn revenue from their creations. This includes avenues such as earning ad revenue and participating in the burgeoning market of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). As we delve further, we'll explore these monetization strategies in more detail to provide a comprehensive understanding of LimeWire's innovative approach to content creation and distribution.


LimeWire Studio welcomes content creators into its fold, providing a space to craft personalized AI-focused content for sharing with fans and followers. Within this creative hub, every piece of content generated becomes not just a creation but a unique asset—ownable and tradable. Fans have the opportunity to subscribe to creators' pages, immersing themselves in the creative journey and gaining ownership of digital collectibles that hold tradeable value within the LimeWire community. Notably, creators earn a 2.5% royalty each time their content is traded, adding a rewarding element to the creative process.


The platform's flexibility is evident in its content publication options. Creators can choose to share their work freely with the public or opt for a premium subscription model, granting exclusive access to specialized content for subscribers.


LimeWire AI Studio

As of the present moment, LimeWire focuses on AI Image Generation, offering a spectrum of creative possibilities to its user base. The platform, however, has ambitious plans on the horizon, aiming to broaden its offerings by introducing AI music and video generation tools in the near future. This strategic expansion promises creators even more avenues for expression and engagement with their audience, positioning LimeWire Studio as a dynamic and evolving platform within the realm of AI-powered content creation.


AI Image Generation Tools



The LimeWire AI image generation tool presents a versatile platform for both the creation and editing of images. Supporting advanced models such as Stable Diffusion 2.1, Stable Diffusion XL, and DALL-E 2, LimeWire offers a sophisticated toolkit for users to delve into the realm of generative AI art.


Much like other tools in the generative AI landscape, LimeWire provides a range of options catering to various levels of complexity in image creation. Users can initiate the creative process with prompts as simple as a few words or opt for more intricate instructions, tailoring the output to their artistic vision.


What sets LimeWire apart is its seamless integration of different AI models and design styles. Users have the flexibility to effortlessly switch between various AI models, exploring diverse design styles such as cinematic, digital art, pixel art, anime, analog film, and more. Each style imparts a distinctive visual identity to the generated AI art, enabling users to explore a broad spectrum of creative possibilities.


The platform also offers additional features, including samplers, allowing users to fine-tune the quality and detail levels of their creations. Customization options and prompt guidance further enhance the user experience, providing a user-friendly interface for both novice and experienced creators.


Excitingly, LimeWire is actively developing its proprietary AI model, signaling ongoing innovation and enhancements to its image generation capabilities. This upcoming addition holds the promise of further expanding the creative horizons for LimeWire users, making it an evolving and dynamic platform within the landscape of AI-driven art and image creation.

Sign Up Now To Get Free Credits

Automatically Mint Your Content As NFTs



Upon completing your creative endeavor on LimeWire, the platform allows you the option to publish your content. An intriguing feature follows this step: LimeWire automates the process of minting your creation as a Non-Fungible Token (NFT), utilizing either the Polygon or Algorand blockchain. This transformative step imbues your artwork with a unique digital signature, securing its authenticity and ownership in the decentralized realm.


Creators on LimeWire hold the power to decide the accessibility of their NFT creations. By opting for a public release, the content becomes discoverable by anyone, fostering a space for engagement and interaction. Furthermore, this choice opens the avenue for enthusiasts to trade the NFTs, adding a layer of community involvement to the artistic journey.


Alternatively, LimeWire acknowledges the importance of exclusivity. Creators can choose to share their posts exclusively with their premium subscribers. In doing so, the content remains a special offering solely for dedicated fans, creating an intimate and personalized experience within the LimeWire community. This flexibility in sharing options emphasizes LimeWire's commitment to empowering creators with choices in how they connect with their audience and distribute their digital creations.


After creating your content, you can choose to publish the content. It will automatically mint your creation as an NFT on the Polygon or Algorand blockchain. You can also choose whether to make it public or subscriber-only.


If you make it public, anyone can discover your content and even trade the NFTs. If you choose to share the post only with your premium subscribers, it will be exclusive only to your fans.


Earn Revenue From Your Content

Additionally, you can earn ad revenue from your content creations as well.

When you publish content on LimeWire, you will receive 70% of all ad revenue from other users who view your images, music, and videos on the platform.


This revenue model will be much more beneficial to designers. You can experiment with the AI image and content generation tools and share your creations while earning a small income on the side.


LMWR Tokens

The revenue you earn from your creations will come in the form of LMWR tokens, LimeWire’s own cryptocurrency.

Your earnings will be paid every month in LMWR, which you can then trade on many popular crypto exchange platforms like Kraken, ByBit, and UniSwap.

You can also use your LMWR tokens to pay for prompts when using LimeWire generative AI tools.

Pricing Plans

You can sign up to LimeWire to use its AI tools for free. You will receive 10 credits to use and generate up to 20 AI images per day. You will also receive 50% of the ad revenue share. However, you will get more benefits with premium plans.

  • Basic plan: 

For $9.99 per month, you will get 1,000 credits per month, up to 2 ,000 image generations, early access to new AI models, and 50% ad revenue share

  • Advanced plan: 

For $29 per month, you will get 3750 credits per month, up to 7500 image generations, early access to new AI models, and 60% ad revenue share

  • Pro plan: 

For $49 per month, you will get 5,000 credits per month, up to 10,000 image generations, early access to new AI models, and 70% ad revenue share

  • Pro Plus plan: 

For $99 per month, you will get 11,250 credits per month, up to 2 2,500 image generations, early access to new AI models, and 70% ad revenue share

With all premium plans, you will receive a Pro profile badge, full creation history, faster image generation, and no ads.

Sign Up Now To Get Free Credits

Conclusion

In conclusion, LimeWire emerges as a democratizing force in the creative landscape, providing an inclusive platform where anyone can unleash their artistic potential and effortlessly share their work. With the integration of AI, LimeWire eliminates traditional barriers, empowering designers, musicians, and artists to publish their creations and earn revenue with just a few clicks.


The ongoing commitment of LimeWire to innovation is evident in its plans to enhance generative AI tools with new features and models. The upcoming expansion to include music and video generation tools holds the promise of unlocking even more possibilities for creators. It sparks anticipation about the diverse and innovative ways in which artists will leverage these tools to produce and publish their own unique creations.


For those eager to explore, LimeWire's AI tools are readily accessible for free, providing an opportunity to experiment and delve into the world of generative art. As LimeWire continues to evolve, creators are encouraged to stay tuned for the launch of its forthcoming AI music and video generation tools, promising a future brimming with creative potential and endless artistic exploration

#9713. 17 apple dessert recipes for fall baking: Embrace the season with apple tarts, cookies, cakes, and more.

There’s an apple dessert for everyone. For the purists, there are lattice-topped pies and shingled galettes. For the non-traditionalists, there are caramel-frosted cakes and fritter-inspired loaves. And for apple lovers that hate cinnamon? Well, there are custardy cakes and classic French tarts. Ready to start baking with fall’s best fruit? Read on for our best apple dessert recipes.

There’s no shortage of apple in this cake — applesauce keeps things moist while boiled cider adds sharp, tangy fruit flavor. The cake is great on its own, but pair it with light, creamy Whipped Caramel Frosting, and you’ve got an irresistible baked version of a caramel apple (with none of the fears about your teeth).

Get the recipe: Whipped Caramel Apple Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vermont Boiled Cider

You only need one apple (and two people eager for an apple dessert) to make a pair of these adorable galettes. Half the apple is sliced, while the other half is grated, which creates a hidden layer of jam beneath the shingled slices. Flaky fruit tarts don’t get easier (or cuter!) than this.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

Get the recipe: Apple Cider Snickerdoodles

This super-easy one-bowl cake is loaded with chopped apples and walnuts, which give this moist, spiced cake heft and texture. The frosting, akin to a velvety brown sugar fudge, adds a textural counterpoint and an extra dimension of richness.

Get the recipe: Old-Fashioned Apple Cake with Brown Sugar Frosting

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" x 13" pan

Cinnamon and apple go together like a flannel and a beanie, but this recipe one-ups that perfect pairing with the addition of cinnamon chips. Diced apple and melty pockets of cinnamon-sugar are also studded throughout these autumnal scones, which are then finished off with an extra-crunchy sugar coating.

Get the recipe: Fresh Apple Cinnamon Scones

To make this recipe, you'll need: Cinnamon Sweet Bits

Ribbons of gooey, cinnamon-scented apples are twisted throughout this striking enriched loaf. Beautiful to behold (and easier to make than you’d think), this braided babka would be a welcome addition to any Rosh Hashanah table or fall celebration.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk

Spoiler alert: The eponymous secret ingredient in this special pie is boiled cider! Made by cooking down apple cider into a concentrate, a few drops deliver big apple flavor. When used in apple pies, it super-charges the fruit’s tart, tangy flavor, delivering a pie with over-the-top apple goodness.

Get the recipe: Secret Ingredient Apple Pie

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider

If your go-to doughnut order is an apple fritter, this mash-up cake was made for you. The batter is made using the reverse creaming technique, which ensures a velvety crumb and tender texture. In each slice, there’s a filling and topping of cinnamon-dusted apples and a final drizzle of icy-white vanilla glaze. A slice rivals anything you can get at your local doughnut shop.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant ClearJel

This time of year, apples don't need much to make them shine. The paper-thin, crackly top layer of this cobbler highlights the juicy fruit beneath. It doesn’t need a lot of adornment, but a scoop of vanilla ice cream never hurt anything.

Get the recipe: Sugar-Crusted Apple Cobbler Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon

Is it a bar? A slab pie? Both! This breezy recipe swaps the flaky pastry for a buttery shortbread crust but keeps the warm, gooey apples and classic spices for a sliceable, portable dessert. To finish, there's a crumbly streusel topping inspired by Dutch apple pie.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

When you want a fruit dessert fast, you can always count on crisps — no rolling, no resting, and most importantly, no special equipment required! This crisp is made with a handful of baking basics, so when you find yourself with a surplus of apples, dessert is barely an hour away.

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" Square Pan

Beneath a buttery, apple-pie-spiced streusel lies a generous layer of tender apples, enriched with intensely flavored boiled cider for a filling that tastes like a truly great apple pie — rich, saucy, and fork-tender apples. The sour cream cake that surrounds the apple filling is plush, subtly tangy, and ultra-moist, providing the perfect counterpoint to the fruit filling and crumb topping.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

If you’re looking to veer from classic apple pie territory, this galette stays true to those roots but adds a few modern twists. It starts with a buttery whole wheat crust enriched with a touch of sour cream. Then, a layer of apple butter (which can be easily made by cooking down applesauce) is spread beneath a layer of artfully arranged apples slices.

Get the recipe: Apple Butter Apple Galette

To make this recipe, you'll need: Sparkling Sugar

There’s just enough batter to hold together a heap of sliced apples in this one-of-a-kind cake. Gently sweetened with brown sugar and scented with almond extract, this minimalist cake is greater than the sum of its parts — a sophisticated, custardy cake that’s deceivingly simple to make.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Almond Extract

This pull-apart bread is as fun to make as it is to eat. After rolling out the dough into a rectangle, it’s spread with sweetened apple filling. The dough is cut up into several strips, then stacked and squeezed into a loaf pan. It bakes into a loaf comprised of distinct slices of pillowy apple-studded bread that you can easily tear from the loaf.

Get the recipe: Cinnamon-Apple Pull-Apart Bread

To make this recipe, you'll need: SAF Instant Yeast

The French know a thing or two about baking with apples, and perhaps no recipe is as classic — or elegant — as the Tarte Tatin. Comprised of deeply caramelized apples layered over buttery pastry, it’s a dessert that stuns. Here, we've tested endlessly to ensure this sometimes-fussy dessert goes off without a hitch in your home kitchen.

Get the recipe: Classic Apple Tarte Tatin

To make this recipe, you'll need: King Arthur Round Cake Pan

These handheld treats harness all the nostalgia of a steaming hot McDonald’s fried apple pie but are infinitely better, thanks to the triple threat of a homemade flaky pie crust, a fresh apple filling amplified by boiled cider, and a generous coating of cinnamon sugar.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice

Looking for more fall baking inspiration? Check out our recipe collection of Fall Favorites.

#9707. Is a gas oven bad for bread?: Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.

Adapted from King Arthur Baking Company’s Big Book of Bread

One of the most crucial steps for making crusty artisan-style bread comes at the very end: steaming.

Baking bread with steam is critical for achieving expansive, open-crumbed loaves with a golden, crisp crust. If you bake bread in a dry oven, the crust quickly sets, which prevents the dough from expanding to its full potential; this, in turn, leads to loaves with a denser crumb. If you introduce steam at the start of the bake, the crust remains moist and pliable and the loaf can stretch and expand before the crust sets, resulting in a lighter, more open crumb.

What’s more, steam also helps gelatinize starches on the loaf’s exterior, which helps it brown and creates an especially crispy, flavorful, and shiny loaf. (Learn more: A guide to baking bread with steam at home.)

There are many different ways to steam your bread, all of which are designed to introduce moisture to the oven during the first part of baking. The most common method involves setting a large cast-iron skillet below your baking stone or steel when you preheat the oven. After you load your bread into the oven, you immediately pour a cup or so of warm water into the preheated cast-iron skillet and quickly close the door so the steam doesn’t escape.

This method works great, with one exception: It’s not effective in a gas oven.

If you have a gas oven, it’s very hard to add sufficient steam. By design, gas ovens vent out effluence, meaning whatever steam you add is very quickly vented out of the oven chamber. This is particularly true if you steam your bread by pouring hot water into a cast-iron skillet, as outlined above. All the water quickly dissipates, and there’s not enough moisture left to enhance the crust.

But all is not lost. There is a workaround.

If you’re steaming bread in a gas oven, you need to use a preheated covered baker, such as a Dutch oven. Instead of adding an additional water source, the lidded vessel traps the steam that escapes from the loaf as it bakes, becoming a kind of self-steaming oven. Because the steam is sealed in, the gas oven won’t vent it out.

You can use a Dutch oven for a round, boule-shaped loaf, or any other form of covered baker, like the Brod & Taylor Bread Steel for elongated, bâtard-shaped loaves. (There’s also a round version of the Bread Steel available.)

For more guidance on this method, see our previous blogs, Bread baking in a Dutch oven and For crispy, crackle crusts, put a lid on it.

When you load your dough into the oven, slip a few ice cubes between the parchment beneath your loaf and the pan to give the loaf an extra initial burst of steam. Just don’t skip the parchment beneath the dough. Otherwise, the extra water from the melting ice may cause your bread to stick to the pot.

Cover photo and food styling by Martin Philip.
